The Hessian hypothesis makes the last term at least $\mu\|y-x\|_2^2/2$, proving the first inequality. Since $H_f\succeq\mu I\succeq0$, [F2] also makes $f$ convex on $U$.

Let $x^*$ be an interior minimizer. For each standard basis vector $e_j$, openness gives an interval around $0$ on which $x^*+te_j\in U$. The one-variable function $t\mapsto f(x^*+te_j)$ has a minimum at $0$, so its derivative there is $0$; [F4] identifies this derivative with $\partial_j f(x^*)$. Thus every coordinate of $\nabla f(x^*)$ is zero.
Apply the first inequality from step 1.1 once to $(x,y)$ and once to $(y,x)$, and add. The function-value terms cancel, leaving $\langle\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\ge\mu\|y-x\|_2^2$.

Apply step 1.1 with the ordered pair $(x,x^*)$ and write $d:=x-x^*$. Rearrangement gives $f(x)-f^*\le\langle
abla f(x),dangle-\mu\|d\|_2^2/2$. By [F5] and completing the square, the right-hand side is at most $\|
abla f(x)\|_2^2/(2\mu)$, since $0\le(\|
abla f(x)\|_2-\mu\|d\|_2)^2$. This is the gradient-gap inequality.
